headline: Parking at the Fairy Pools
reservation: Access to the site does not currently require a permit, but parking is managed by the Outdoor Access Trust for Scotland. Visitors should check the official trust site for current parking fees and seasonal availability as site management can change.

days.title: Crystal Pools of Skye

stops.name: Fairy Pools
stops.detail: Explore the series of vivid blue rock pools and waterfalls fed by the Brittle River.

days.driving: Allow 20-30 minutes; mountain road conditions and passing place availability vary.
days.note: Pace your walk to account for variable weather and rocky terrain near the water.

intel.title: Vehicle Size Limits
intel.text: A designated parking area exists for larger vehicles. Motorhomes and other large vehicles are strictly limited to a maximum length of 8 metres.

intel.title: Mobile Connectivity
intel.text: Evidence does not specify signal strength in this remote glen. Verify offline map availability before departing from local towns.

intel.title: Local Supplies
intel.text: No fuel is listed at the site. Ensure the tank is sufficient for the return trip to nearby villages like Carbost or Portree.

intel.title: Visit Duration
intel.text: The length of stay depends on walking speed and weather. Allow several hours to reach the upper pools and return to the parking area.

intel.title: Trail Conditions
intel.text: Access involves a walk from the designated car park. Check local weather reports as the path can be affected by heavy rainfall.

plan.arrival: Arrive via the A863 and B8009, following local signage toward Glenbrittle. The parking area is the primary access point for the trail.
plan.vehicle: Suitable for cars and motorhomes under 8 metres. Check rental agreements for driving on single-track roads with passing places.
plan.goldenHour: The pools sit in the shadow of the Black Cuillin; sunset light varies significantly with the season.
